text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on April 24 in history:
1533 - William the Silent, Prince of Orange, born. He led the revolt against Spanish rule and helped create an autonomous Netherlands.
1558 - Mary Queen of Scots, aged 16, married the Dauphin of France, the future Francis II.
1704 - The Boston News-Letter, one of the earliest newspapers in the American colonies, was first published.
1731 - Daniel Defoe, British journalist and author, notably of "Robinson Crusoe", died.
1800 - The U.S. Congress voted to establish a Library of Congress.

1815 - Anthony Trollope, English novelist, born. Worked as a junior clerk in the Post Office until he began writing in the 1840s. Best known for the Barchester novels, a series of books set in the fictional English county of Barsetshire.

1856 - Philippe Petain, French statesman and army marshal, born. A national hero for his victory at Verdun in the First World War, he was discredited as a collaborator for setting up the Vichy government in World War two.
1882 - Lord Dowding, British air force commander who directed the Battle of Britain, born.
1889 - Stafford Cripps, British statesman and chancellor of the exchequer after World War Two, born. As chancellor, he was noted for his policy of austerity.
1905 - Robert Penn Warren, U.S. poet and novelist notably of "All The King's Men", born.
1906 - William Joyce, U.S.-born British collaborator during World War Two, born. He was best known for his radio broadcasts of Nazi propaganda from Germany under his nickname "Lord Haw-Haw".
1916 - The Easter Rising in Dublin, an insurrection aimed at setting up an Irish Republic, began.
1921 - The Tyrol region of central Europe voted for union with Germany.
1932 - In German elections, the Nazis had election successes in Prussia, Bavaria, Wurttemberg and Hamburg.
1934 - Shirley MacLaine, U.S. actress, dancer and sister of Warren Beatty, born as Shirley MacLean Beaty.
1939 - Robert Menzies became Australian prime minister, succeeding Joseph Lyons who died earlier in the month.
1942 - Barbra Streisand, American actress and singer, born.
1945 - U.S. forces liberated Dachau concentration camp.
1950 - The state of Jordan was formed by the union of Jordanian-occupied Palestine and the Kingdom of Transjordan.
1955 - The Bandung Conference, organised by five Asian states, ended. It condemned colonialism by both the West and the USSR.
1965 - The body of murdered Portuguese opposition leader Humberto Delgado was found in Spain.
1965 - The government of Indonesia formally took control of all foreign companies in the country.
1967 - Vladimir Komarov, the first Russian to fly in the Soyuz craft, was killed when he crash-landed in Russia after his 17th orbit of Earth.
1970 - Gambia was proclaimed a republic within the British Commonwealth.
1970 - China launched its first satellite into orbit.
1975 - Three people died when Baader-Meinhof terrorists attacked the German embassy in Stockholm, Sweden.
1986 - The Duchess of Windsor (Wallis Warfield) died. As Wallis Simpson, her romance with King Edward VIII led to his abdication in 1936.
1990 - East and West Germany agreed on July 2 as the date for economic union, a prelude to full political unification.
1991 - Kurdish rebel leaders reached an agreement in principle with Saddam Hussein on greater autonomy.
1992 - Guerrilla leaders in Afghanistan agreed on a 50-member council to take power in Kabul.
1993 - A huge IRA bomb exploded in Bishopgate, in the heart of London's financial district, killing one person.
1995 - The U.N. tribunal for former Yugoslavia named Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic and two of his senior aides as war crimes suspects.
1996 - The Palestinian parliament-in-exile voted to amend clauses in the PLO charter which call for Israel's destruction.
1996 - Russian President Boris Yeltsin met Chinese President Jiang Zemin at the start of a visit to Beijing both leaders hailed as signalling a new spring between the giant neighbours.
